test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Graduate Level) Official Paper (Held On: 25 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: From the summit of a 100 m high cliff, the angles of depression to two boats situated on the same side of the cliff are measured at 30° and 45° respectively. The boats are moving towards the cliff in a straight line. After 5 minutes, the angle of depression to the first boat becomes 60°, while the angle to the second boat becomes 75°. If both boats move at constant but different speeds, determine the initial distance between the two boats.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial Distance (d) = Cliff Height × (cot θₛₘₐₗₗₑᵣ − cot θₗₐᵣgₑᵣ)

Here, Height = 100 m, θₛₘₐₗₗₑᵣ = 30°, θₗₐᵣgₑᵣ = 45°

d = 100 × (cot 30° − cot 45°)

d = 100 × (√3 − 1) = 100 × (1.732 − 1) = 100 × 0.732

d = 73.2 m

**∴ The correct option is (1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of cliff (AB) = 100 m

Initial angles of depression = 30° and 45°

**Formula Used:**

In right-angled triangle, tan θ = Perpendicular / Base ⇒ Base = Perpendicular / tan θ = Perpendicular × cot θ

Let B be the base of the cliff and A be the summit.

Let Boat 1 be at D and Boat 2 be at C on the same side of the cliff.

Initial Position of Boat 2 (C) at 45°:

⇒ In ΔABC, cot 45° = BC / AB

⇒ 1 = BC / 100

⇒ BC = 100 m

Initial Position of Boat 1 (D) at 30°:

⇒ In ΔABD, cot 30° = BD / AB

⇒ √3 = BD / 100

⇒ BD = 100√3 m

Initial distance between the two boats (CD):

⇒ CD = BD − BC

⇒ CD = 100√3 − 100

⇒ CD = 100(1.732 − 1)

⇒ CD = 100 × 0.732 = 73.2 m

**∴ The correct option is (1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Depression

The angle formed between the horizontal line of sight and the object when the object is below the eye level. Angle of Depression = Angle of Elevation due to parallel horizontal lines.

Trigonometric Distance Formula

When an observer at height h sees two objects with angles of elevation α and β (α < β) on the same side, the distance between them is d = h(cot α − cot β).

Common Angle Values

cot 30° = √3 ≈ 1.732, cot 45° = 1, cot 60° = 1/√3 ≈ 0.577, cot 75° = 2 − √3 ≈ 0.268.</p
